page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DSv4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It features an L3 cache size of 35 MB, alongside L1d and L2 caches of 32 KB and 1.0 MB respectively. This instance is Premium Storage capable but does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark evaluations place the D8s_v4 consistently in the average performance tier across most workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests yield scores of 1411.98 and 7435.42, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 414.43 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 44.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 32.6 GB/sec for large-block writes. In Geekbench testing, the instance scores 1155.0 in single-core and 4610.0 in multi-core tests, with average performance in software compilation (6834.0) and ray tracing (6357.0). However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in bzip3 decompression, scoring 8.78 GB/sec single-threaded and 25.34 GB/sec multi-threaded, as well as in small LLM prompt processing (380.28 tokens/sec).

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v4 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a stable resource density for standard enterprise applications. Given its average performance in database operations (2861.21 on Passmark) and static web serving throughput (6.85 GB/sec), this instance is best suited for general-purpose application hosting, software compilation, Redis caching (delivering 6.84 million operations per second), and moderate web serving.
